correctness.rationale: The rank-three affine matroid independence complex is a wedge of two-spheres by published matroid shellability. The nonzero translation prime-order stabilizer test is exhaustive for faces of sizes 1–3: characteristic three triples are collinear, characteristic two fixed points are precisely \(q^2/2\) swapped-edge midpoints. The finite-group orbit-space \(\pi_1\) theorem yields \(T/N\). Exact f-vector and Burnside Euler computations yield the \(b_2\) formula; 2-dimensional cellular chains make \(H_2\) free, and \(H_1\) finite makes its rational rank vanish. Even characteristic yields a wedge-of-spheres homotopy equivalence by Hurewicz and Whitehead. Standalone exact integral Smith computations for \(q=2,3,4\) agree, including \((\mathbb Z/3)^2\) at \(q=3\), with explicit chain matrices and verified boundary composition. No finite observation is substituted for the infinite proof.
residual_risks: The proof uses the classical Armstrong orbit-space theorem rather than giving a new proof of that general theorem; its applicability is checked by barycentric subdivision and simple connectivity.

value.rationale: This is a natural infinite family of all finite-field affine-plane rank-three matroid complexes under their regular translation group, rather than an artificial slice. It gives a complete integral homology classification and a full even-characteristic homotopy classification. A geometric stabilizer transition exactly at characteristic two transforms a nontrivial odd-characteristic elementary-abelian fundamental group of unbounded prime exponent into a simply connected wedge of two-spheres. The arithmetic mechanism and explicit Betti ranks are useful structural information not obtained from cover shellability or rational representations alone.
residual_risks: The full odd-characteristic homotopy two-type remains unspecified; that does not limit the exact fundamental-group and integral-homology theorem.
